messages.author: 5170c59f79bda4af
messages.subject: idata.frame behavior change?
parts:
Hi all,

It is possible I was using idata.frame incorrectly to begin with, but a piece of code that used to work well for me is no longer working as of today, when I updated from R 2.15.0 to 2.15.2 . What's the story here? Happy to post example data, but in short, the code looks like this:

result <- ddply(idata.frame(input.data), c("category1","category2"), summarise, statistic1=length(variableOfInterest), statistic2=sum(variableOfInterest))

And I get this error: Error in sum(variableOfInterest) : invalid 'type' (closure) of argument

This code, however, seems to work on a smaller version of the input data, though it runs very slowly on the actual large data frame:

result <- ddply(input.data, c("category1","category2"), summarise, variable1=length(variableOfInterest), variable2=sum(variableOfInterest))

Any help would be greatly appreciated.

Cheers,
Eliot

messages.author: 5170c59f79bda4af
messages.subject: Re: idata.frame behavior change?
parts:
A brief update to confirm that the code works well without the idata.frame component. Subsequent lines of code that also used to run--calls of ddply() on idf objects--also failed, e.g.:

> bio1niche <- ddply(idata.frame(combo.onehund), "species", summarise, niche=mean(bio1mean))
There were 50 or more warnings (use warnings() to see the first 50)
> warnings()
Warning messages:
1: In mean.default(bio1mean) : argument is not numeric or logical: returning NA

messages.subject: Re: idata.frame behavior change?
parts:
Hi Hadley,

Absolutely. Apologies that I don't know how to best insert code into these emails, but this reproduces the problem on my computer. The second ddply statement gives the error: Error in sum(count) : invalid 'type' (closure) of argument

###################

species <- c("Species1","Species1","Species1","Species2","Species2","Species4","Species5","Species5")
count <- c(10,6,3,2,2,3,15,10)
grid <- c(1,2,3,1,2,2,3,3)

input <- data.frame(species,count,grid)

ddply(input, c("grid","species"), summarise, occurrences=length(count), count=sum(count))

ddply(idata.frame(input), c("grid","species"), summarise, occurrences=length(count), count=sum(count))


###############

Cheers,
Eliot
